title: Osso Buco
subtitle: Braised beef shin with gremolata
excerpt: Cross-cut beef shin braised for two and a half hours in a soffritto of onion, carrot and celery with white wine and tomatoes, finished with a bright gremolata of lemon zest, garlic and parsley. The marrow inside the bone is one of the rewards of the dish; scoop it out with a small spoon and eat it with the braising sauce. Serve over polenta or with crusty bread.
sourceNotes: Osso buco is a Milanese speciality dating to the 19th century; the name means 'bone with a hole' and refers to the marrow-filled cross-cut of veal shin, though beef shin is a widely used and accessible substitute.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze braised shin in its sauce for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently. Add gremolata fresh.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The braise can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat gently on the hob. Make the gremolata fresh on the day.

content.text: Ask your butcher for cross-cut beef shin rounds, about 4 to 5cm thick. These are often labelled as osso buco cuts. Tying a piece of kitchen twine around each round holds the meat together during the long braise and keeps it looking neat when served. The gremolata goes on at the very last moment; it is meant to be raw and bright, a contrast to the richness of the braise below it.

items.prepNote: cross-cut into thick rounds, ask your butcher for osso buco cuts
4 cloves crushed for the braise, 1 clove finely minced for the gremolata
for dusting the beef before browning

content.text: Heat the oven to 160C (fan 140C / Gas 3). Season the shin rounds generously, then dust all sides in flour, patting off any excess. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over a high heat. Brown the shin rounds for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply coloured. Remove to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil to the pot, then cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes until softened and beginning to colour. Add the 4 crushed garlic cloves and tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Stir, then nestle the browned shin rounds back into the pot. Tuck in the bay leaves and thyme sprigs. The liquid should come about halfway up the meat.

Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and transfer to the oven. Braise for 2 hours to 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is very tender and falling away from the bone. Check halfway through and add a splash of water if the sauce looks too reduced.

Make the gremolata: mix the finely minced garlic clove, lemon zest and finely chopped parsley together. Serve the osso buco over polenta or with crusty bread, with the gremolata scattered generously over the top. The marrow inside the bone is excellent scooped out with a small spoon and stirred into the sauce.

items.symptom: Meat is still tough after 2.5 hours
items.cause: Shin requires very long cooking; the oven temperature may be slightly low
items.fix: Return to the oven for another 30 to 45 minutes. The meat must be fork-tender to the point where it almost falls off the bone before it is done.

items.symptom: Sauce has reduced to almost nothing
items.cause: Lid was not sealed tightly enough or oven temperature was too high
items.fix: Add 200ml of hot water or stock, stir gently and continue cooking. Next time ensure the lid fits snugly or cover the pot with foil before adding the lid.
